actionable_findings.title: Option equality XML falsely declares invalid default state
actionable_findings.why_it_matters: Consumers reading the shipped equality documentation are told that a default Option operand throws InvalidOperationException, although default Option is the valid None value: default(Option<int>) == Option<int>.None returns true and the corresponding inequality returns false. Both newly added exception elements contradict the implementation and the C:218/C:219 stable API crosswalk, leaving the Goal 24 exception/XML contract repair inaccurate for these public members. Removing the two invalid-state exception claims preserves the accepted default-as-None behavior and keeps user-comparer exceptions distinct from a nonexistent carrier initialization guard.
actionable_findings.validation_reason: When either equality operand is default Option<T>, Option.cs:118 defines that state as legal None and lines 420-443 compare its false IsSome tag without an initialization guard, so the diff-added InvalidOperationException claims at lines 436 and 442 misdocument shipped operator behavior and contradict R9 and stable crosswalk rows C:218/C:219; the supporting OptionTests were inspected but not executed.
